name: Applying & Converting Sigma Rules — sigmac, Chainsaw, pySigma & Splunk
description: Converting Sigma rules to SIEM queries and applying them to event logs. sigmac (legacy): python sigmac -t <backend> rule.yml [-c config.yml]. Backends: powershell, splunk, es-qs, qradar. Chainsaw hunt: chainsaw_x86_64.exe hunt <evtx_path> -s <sigma_rule_or_dir> --mapping mappings/sigma-event-logs-all.yml. Mapping files tell Chainsaw which event log fields to use — missing fields cause 0 detections even when rules are correct. pySigma / Uncoder.io = modern sigmac alternatives. Config files critical: sigma-event-logs-all.yml may need custom fields added (e.g., NewProcessName for EID 4688). Zircolite: alternative to Chainsaw for EVTX+Sigma hunting.
source: CDSA Module 12: YARA & Sigma for SOC Analysts
notes:
=== sigmac — SIGMA RULE CONVERTER (LEGACY) ===

sigmac converts Sigma YAML rules into SIEM-specific query language.
Location in lab: C:\Tools\sigma-0.21\tools\sigmac

Basic syntax:
  python sigmac -t <backend> <rule.yml> [-c <config.yml>]

Common backends (-t):
  powershell    → Get-WinEvent PowerShell query
  splunk        → Splunk SPL search
  es-qs         → Elasticsearch Query String
  es-dsl        → Elasticsearch DSL (JSON)
  qradar        → IBM QRadar AQL
  logpoint      → LogPoint query
  arcsight      → ArcSight filter

--- Convert to PowerShell (Get-WinEvent): ---
  python sigmac -t powershell 'C:\Rules\sigma\proc_access_win_lsass_access.yml'

  Output:
    Get-WinEvent | where {
      ($_.ID -eq "10" -and
       $_.message -match "TargetImage.*.*\\lsass.exe" -and
       $_.message -match "GrantedAccess.*.*0x1010")
    } | select TimeCreated,Id,RecordId,ProcessId,MachineName,Message

--- Run Get-WinEvent against specific .evtx file: ---
  Get-WinEvent -Path C:\Events\YARASigma\lab_events.evtx | where {
    ($_.ID -eq "10" -and
     $_.message -match "TargetImage.*.*\\lsass.exe" -and
     $_.message -match "GrantedAccess.*.*0x1010")
  } | select TimeCreated,Id,RecordId,ProcessId,MachineName,Message

  Note: Run PowerShell as Administrator for EVTX access.

--- Convert to Splunk: ---
  python sigmac -t splunk 'C:\Tools\chainsaw\sigma\rules\windows\process_access\proc_access_win_lsass_dump_comsvcs_dll.yml' -c .\config\splunk-windows.yml

  Output:
    (TargetImage="*\\lsass.exe" SourceImage="C:\\Windows\\System32\\rundll32.exe" CallTrace="*comsvcs.dll*")

  Note: -c config/splunk-windows.yml maps Sigma field names to Splunk field names
  Sysmon + Splunk Universal Forwarder required for data ingestion

--- Convert notepad susp child process rule to Splunk: ---
  python sigmac -t splunk 'C:\Rules\sigma\proc_creation_win_notepad_susp_child.yml' -c .\config\splunk-windows.yml

  Output:
    (ParentImage="*\\notepad.exe" (Image="*\\powershell.exe" OR Image="*\\cmd.exe" OR ...))

=== SIGMAC CONFIG FILES ===
Location: C:\Tools\sigma-0.21\tools\config\
  splunk-windows.yml    → maps Sigma fields to Splunk fields for Windows
  sysmon.yml            → Sysmon-specific field mappings
  elasticsearch.yml     → ES field mappings

Config file format (YAML):
  fieldmappings:
    Image: NewProcessName           ← Sigma field → EVTX/SIEM field
    CommandLine: ProcessCommandLine
    ParentImage: ParentProcessName

Critical: without correct config, queries reference wrong field names
  → Always specify -c <config> for production use
  → Custom config needed when adding non-standard fields (e.g., NewProcessName for EID 4688)

=== pySigma — MODERN sigmac REPLACEMENT ===
Official modern tool: https://github.com/SigmaHQ/pySigma

  pip install pySigma
  pip install pySigma-backend-splunk    (Splunk backend)
  pip install pySigma-backend-elasticsearch

Convert with pySigma Python API:
  from sigma.collection import SigmaCollection
  from sigma.backends.splunk import SplunkBackend

  rules = SigmaCollection.load_ruleset(["rule.yml"])
  backend = SplunkBackend()
  print(backend.convert(rules))

CLI (via sigma-cli):
  pip install sigma-cli
  sigma convert -t splunk -p windows-sysmon rule.yml

=== Uncoder.io — WEB-BASED SIGMA CONVERTER ===
URL: https://uncoder.io/
  → Paste Sigma YAML → select target SIEM → get converted query
  → Supports: Splunk, Elastic, QRadar, Microsoft Sentinel, Chronicle, etc.
  → No installation required
  → Free tier available

Use case: quick one-off conversions, exploring output formats

=== CHAINSAW — EVENT LOG HUNTING WITH SIGMA ===
Chainsaw applies Sigma rules directly to Windows EVTX files.
No SIEM needed — ideal for incident response.

Location: C:\Tools\chainsaw\chainsaw_x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe

Basic hunt command:
  .\chainsaw_x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe hunt <evtx_path> \
    -s <sigma_rule_or_dir> \
    --mapping mappings\sigma-event-logs-all.yml

Hunt with single rule:
  .\chainsaw_x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe hunt C:\Events\lab_events.evtx \
    -s C:\Rules\sigma\proc_access_win_lsass_access.yml \
    --mapping .\mappings\sigma-event-logs-all.yml

Hunt directory of rules against directory of EVTX:
  .\chainsaw_x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe hunt C:\Events\ \
    -s C:\Tools\chainsaw\sigma\rules\ \
    --mapping .\mappings\sigma-event-logs-all.yml

Hunt with JSON output:
  .\chainsaw_x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe hunt C:\Events\ \
    -s sigma\rules\ \
    --mapping mappings\sigma-event-logs-all.yml \
    --json

--- Mapping files ---
Mappings tell Chainsaw which EVTX fields to use:
  sigma-event-logs-all.yml     → General Windows event log mappings
  sigma-event-logs-all-new.yml → Extended version (includes NewProcessName for EID 4688)

GOTCHA: if a field exists in the Sigma rule but not in the mapping file,
  → Chainsaw returns 0 detections even if rule is logically correct
  → Fix: add the field to the mapping file, or use an extended mapping
  → Example: NewProcessName was missing → 0 detections for EID 4688 rules
             → Added to sigma-event-logs-all-new.yml → detections worked

--- Chainsaw search (keyword hunt): ---
  .\chainsaw_x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe search mimikatz -i C:\Events\

  → -i = case-insensitive
  → Searches raw event log content for keyword

--- Chainsaw search by EventID: ---
  .\chainsaw_x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.exe search -t 'Event.System.EventID: =4104' C:\Events\

--- Chainsaw output format: ---
  Table view by default:
    timestamp | detections | count | Provider | EventID | RecordID | Computer | Event Data

  Use --full flag to show complete event data (not truncated)

=== Zircolite — ALTERNATIVE TO CHAINSAW ===
URL: https://github.com/wagga40/Zircolite
  → Similar to Chainsaw: EVTX + Sigma rules
  → Also scans multiple EVTX files concurrently
  → Output: JSON, CSV, or HTML reports
  → Better suited for large-scale log hunting

Basic usage:
  python3 zircolite.py --evtx C:\Events\ --ruleset sigma\rules\ --outfile results.json

=== SPLUNK SIGMA HUNTING ===
After sigmac conversion, paste SPL into Splunk 'Search & Reporting':
  http://[Target IP]:8000 → Search & Reporting → paste SPL

Splunk searches use tstats or raw field searches:
  (TargetImage="*\\lsass.exe" SourceImage="*\\rundll32.exe" CallTrace="*comsvcs.dll*")
  → Results show events matching all conditions

=== WORKFLOW: SIGMA RULE → HUNT → DETECT ===
1. Write Sigma rule in YAML
2. Convert with sigmac or pySigma to target SIEM format
3. Option A - Quick EVTX hunt:
   chainsaw hunt <evtx> -s rule.yml --mapping mapping.yml
4. Option B - SIEM search:
   Paste converted query into Splunk/Elastic/etc.
5. Option C - PowerShell (no SIEM):
   sigmac -t powershell rule.yml → Get-WinEvent -Path evtx.evtx | where {...}
6. Review hits → confirm true positives
7. Tune rule to reduce false positives
8. Add to detection library
